subject: Next steps: SafeHealth pilot — data residency & training opt-out
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Andrea Lopez <andrea.lopez@safehealth.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@safehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 13:10:00 -0400
Subject: Next steps: SafeHealth pilot — data residency & training opt-out

Hi Andrea / Jordan,

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap and the asks we agreed on: 

- Scope: 6-week pilot for Claims Triage (English only) on a dedicated instance.
- Data residency: pilot data must remain in us-east-1 and not cross regions.
- Logging/retention: access logs retained for 90 days; request/response payloads retained only for 30 days for troubleshooting, then purged.
- PII handling: we will enable strict PII redaction and zero-sample logging for any identified PHI flows.
- Training-on-customer-data: you requested that SafeHealth data NOT be used for model training or improvement. We need a written confirmation to lock this in our onboarding and production configs.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_QA.pdf (security questionnaire stub), SafeHealth_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (template).

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) Andrea to send written confirmation of no-training and residency constraints (this thread).
2) We’ll provision a staging environment in us-east-1 and share a short checklist (infra access + sample data) by EOD Friday.
3) Procurement contact / PO details from Jordan so we can prepare a pilot SOW.

If you can confirm the two items below in reply, we’ll lock the pilot timeline:
- "SafeHealth confirms Redwood may not use pilot data for model training or model improvement."
- "SafeHealth confirms data residency in us-east-1 and the retention windows above."

Thanks — I’ve looped in Rishi (product) for any technical clarifications.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Redwood_Security_QA.pdf (pdf), SafeHealth_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Andrea Lopez <andrea.lopez@safehealth.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps: SafeHealth pilot — data residency & training opt-out

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the two items below on behalf of SafeHealth: 

1) SafeHealth confirms Redwood may NOT use any pilot data, logs, or derived artifacts from this engagement for model training, model improvement, or benchmarking. This applies to all environments (staging/production) for this pilot and any subsequent contracted work unless explicitly renegotiated in writing.

2) SafeHealth confirms data residency requirement: all data and processed artifacts for the pilot must remain in AWS us-east-1; any backups or logging must be stored only in that region.

Additional notes: PII/PHI — we require that request/response payloads that include PHI be redacted prior to any internal viewing. We are okay with limited access by named Redwood personnel for debugging provided an approved Data Access Form is signed.

I’ve attached a marked-up mutual action plan with procurement info (see SafeHealth_MutualActionPlan.xlsx). Jordan is included for PO coordination.

Andrea Lopez
Head of Engineering Operations
SafeHealth
